questions.prompt: `OrderService` depends on `IRepository<Order>` instead of `AppDbContext`. Which benefit from the lesson does that give most directly?
options: Queries run faster because EF Core is bypassed
The database schema is created automatically
The service is easy to unit test, because `IRepository<Order>` can be mocked
questions.explanation: Without a repository, EF Core code is spread everywhere and mocking `DbContext` is painful. Behind `IRepository<T>` the service has no EF Core code and the interface is easy to mock.

questions.prompt: Order the layers a request passes through in the repository pattern structure, from the UI down to the database.
questions.explanation: The UI calls a service, the service talks only to `IRepository<T>`, and the repository implementation uses EF Core's `DbContext` to reach the database.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson register the repository with `AddScoped`?
options: `DbContext` is scoped per request/operation, and the repository should share that lifetime
Scoped services are created only once for the whole application
Generic types can only be registered as scoped
Scoped registration makes `Save()` run automatically at the end of a request
questions.explanation: Under "Why Scoped?" the lesson explains that `DbContext` is scoped per request or operation, so the repository that wraps it should have the same lifetime.

questions.prompt: When would you register a closed generic such as `services.AddScoped<IRepository<Order>, EfRepository<Order>>()` instead of the open generic `typeof(IRepository<>)`?
options: Whenever the app has many entities
When you need special repository logic or a different implementation for one entity
Always, because open generics can't be resolved
questions.explanation: The open generic registration is the best practice for a generic repository with many entities; a closed generic is the special case for one entity or a different implementation per entity.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `services.AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), typeof(OrderRepository));` when `OrderRepository` is not generic?
options: Nothing; it registers `OrderRepository` for every entity
An open generic registration needs a generic implementation
questions.explanation: Registering an open generic with a non-generic implementation is listed as a common mistake: the implementation must also be generic, like `EfRepository<>`.
